newsitem.title: FINLAND: NOKIA SAYS WINS NORWEGIAN TETRA ORDER.
newsitem.headline: NOKIA SAYS WINS NORWEGIAN TETRA ORDER.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy said in a statement on Thursday it had sealed a deal with Olso Energi Tele for delivery of its new trunked mobile radio system (TETRA), but gave no value for the deal.
"This is an important opening but the value is rather small," a Nokia spokeswoman said by telephone.

"Nokia will deliver to Oslo Energi Tele a complete TETRA system and network including a switching centre, base stations, base stations for tunnel communications, network management, Nokia mobile stations and antennas," Nokia said.
Deliveries would begin in December and the network would be in operation at the beginning of 1998, Nokia said.
"Oslo Energi Tele will use Nokia's TETRA system to improve its speach and data communication," Nokia said.

TETRA stands for Trans-European Trunked Radio and is an open digital trunked radio standard for professional mobile radio users such as utlities, oil companies, railways and authorities, it said. The system includes infrastrucutre and mobile radios.
Nokia in January announced a TETRA development deal with the Helsinki City Energy Company.
